verdict.line: You lose when you transform into Mega Gnar in his face and get Q-stunned into a Devour; you win when you poke from Q range and only all-in on your own terms.

brief.thesis: Tahm Kench's Q (Tongue Lash) stacks An Acquired Taste and stuns at 3 stacks, and his E (Thick Skin) turns chip damage into a shield, so he punishes melee auto-trading and outlasts poke unless you burst him in one window. Gnar's ranged Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range) outranges his Q (900 range) and his only gap-closer, W (Abyssal Dive), has a real cooldown you can play around.

tell.watch: Tahm's An Acquired Taste stack count

theirWindow.when: he reaches 3 Acquired Taste stacks on you
theirWindow.what: His next Q (Tongue Lash) stuns and consumes the stacks, and he'll follow with W (Abyssal Dive) or an auto-chain into R (Devour). Back off or pre-commit E (Hop) the moment he's at 2 stacks.

yourWindow.when: right after he uses W (Abyssal Dive)
yourWindow.what: Abyssal Dive is his only dash, on a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown, so once it's used (hit or whiffed) he has zero gap-close for that window. Walk up and poke freely with Q (Boomerang Throw) during it.

powerCurve.note: Q (1100) outranges his Q (900) in poke
W (Abyssal Dive) unlocks forced all-in threat
full builds, his shield matches your burst

start.why: Matches his Q sustain (heals him on hit) early so you aren't losing the poke war on HP alone.

boots.why: Magic resist blunts his Q/W/Devour magic damage and the tenacity shortens his Q slow and stun duration.

core.why: The damage and move speed proc off W (Hyper) lets you poke-and-kite instead of standing in his range.
Armor shred keeps your Q/auto poke relevant as he stacks health for his passive's bonus damage.
The shield and tenacity cover you through his W knockup into a Q stun, and the AD scales as Mega Gnar loses health.

situational.when: he builds tanky and starts snowballing picks off Devour with his jungler
you need more magic resist against his dive-into-Devour burst
the game goes long and his passive health-scaling sustain starts outpacing your poke

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustain and move speed on poke trades fit the kite-don't-melee plan directly. Master-tier Gnar players instead run Lethal Tempo across 3,885 games — that suits players who'd rather commit to extended all-in skirmishes once transformed rather than poke-kite.

summoners.why: Teleport is the standard pick (73.2% pick rate) for scaling into side-lane pressure once your build spikes. Flash+Ignite is worth running instead if you want kill pressure, since Ignite directly cuts his Q heal and E passive sustain, denying his main recovery tools.

playing.title: Poke with Q, never auto-trade
playing.detail: Boomerang Throw's 1100 range beats his 900-range Q, so throw it and walk into the boomerang's return path to cut its cooldown instead of standing in auto range.

playing.title: Hold E once he's at 2 stacks
playing.detail: His passive stacks from Q and autos; at 3 stacks his Q stuns and resets. Keep E (Hop, 22-12s cooldown by rank) free to escape the instant he's one stack from the stun.

playing.title: Attack after his W whiffs or lands
playing.detail: Abyssal Dive is his only dash on a 21-17s cooldown. Once it's spent, he has no way to close distance again for that window — poke freely.

playing.title: Delay your Mega Gnar transform
playing.detail: Rage only builds in combat, so choose when to pop it. Transforming into melee range hands Mega Gnar's E (ground slam) and W (melee stun) to a champion built to punish exactly that.

playing.title: Wall-stun with R once it's online
playing.detail: At rank 3 (level 11) R's cooldown drops to 30s and to 0s at rank 4-5. Throw him into a wall for the bonus stun and damage before he can set up a Devour pick.

playing.title: Save burst for one big window
playing.detail: E (Thick Skin) is on a 3s cooldown and converts stored damage into a shield, so small repeated pokes just feed his shield. Wait for your Trinity Force spike and burst him in one combo instead.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, win rates, and pick rates above come from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning connecting them to specific ability timings and cooldowns is my own tactical read.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid fighting Tahm Kench in melee combat. Use [E] to avoid his (Q) and to create some distance to kite him.
